I wanted a drum machine I could open in a tab and start playing straight away - no install, no account, no sample library to download first. So I built BAP Studio. It is 16 velocity-sensitive pads across four banks, a 16-step sequencer with per-step velocity and swing, four patterns that chain into a song, and a sampler that takes any audio file or mic recording, finds the transients and lays the chops across the pads. Every sound is synthesised in the browser, so there is nothing to install and nothing to wait for. You can export a WAV, a MIDI file, or a link that rebuilds your beat exactly as you left it. Quickest way in: press Space to start the loop, then hit Z, C and A. Most people have something going in about a minute. Would love to hear what you make with it.

# Free, Browser-Based Drum Machine, Shuffle Drummer

Developer Emmanuel Decourt has released Shuffle Drummer, a free, browser-based drum machine and groovebox.

Shuffle Drummer is built on pure Web Audio API, with zero dependencies, so you can just click play or record and start jamming. It offers a drum machine, pad-based triggering, step sequencing, a wide range of effects and more.

You can create an account, which unlocks additional features, including saving, exporting beats as wav files and additional drum kits.

results.content:
Partially. GarageBand (free on Mac and iPhone) is a full music production app with a drum machine, virtual instruments, multi-track recording, and a huge sound library. SoundTools Beat Maker is much more focused — it's a browser-based drum machine and step sequencer, not a full DAW. The advantage: it works on any device including Windows and Android with no download, no account, and no setup. If you want to make a quick drum beat, export it, and get on with your day, SoundTools is faster. If you want to produce a full song with multiple instruments, GarageBand (or BandLab on any device) is the right tool.

### Is this a BandLab alternative? [...] ### Is this a BandLab alternative?

For beat making specifically, yes. BandLab is a full free online DAW with multi-track recording, virtual instruments, and a social sharing platform — and it's excellent. SoundTools Beat Maker is narrower in scope: a drum machine and step sequencer focused on quickly building and exporting drum patterns. SoundTools requires no account at all, loads instantly, and keeps everything in your browser. If you want to sketch a drum loop fast and export a WAV, SoundTools is quicker to get in and out of. If you want to build a full song, record vocals, and collaborate with others, BandLab is the better platform.

## Drum Pad, Beat Pad, Drum Machine — One Free Tool

SoundTools Beat Maker is a free online drum pad — also called a beat pad, drumpad, or sample pad — combined with a full drum machine and step sequencer, running entirely in your browser. It gives you 16 playable pads, seven classic drum machine kits, and the ability to record your own sounds using your microphone. No account, no download, no upload required — just open the page and start tapping.

The tool has two modes.

### Beat Pad Mode: Tap and Play

Drum Pad mode gives you a grid of 16 colorful pads you can tap or click to play drum sounds instantly — this is the classic beat pad experience, and you can use keyboard shortcuts (Q-W-E-R, A-S-D-F, Z-X-C-V) to finger-drum like a pro.

# Online drum machine

## What is a drum machine?

A drum machine is an electronic musical instrument that can imitate drum kits and percussion instruments. Some can also produce artificial sound effects. Most drum machines allow users to create their own beats.

A drum machine is commonly used for recording electronic music, often used in house, dance, and hip hop genres. It may also be used as a metronome, as a backing track for practice or as a way to explore a variety of drum rhythms.

Drumbit.app is a versatile, free, web-based drum sequencer. There are lots of pre-set rhythm (beat) patterns to choose from and many different effects too. It allows the user to program four separate four-beat patterns to complete a phrase. The swing and BPM can be adjusted overall, as well as the pitch and volume for each track. This means each instrument track can be customized to find that perfect sound. ‘Keys Mode’ allows the user to manipulate the machine’s rhythm blocks with their computer’s QWERTY keyboard. Projects can be saved in JSON format; a web file that can be downloaded to a hard drive and then uploaded to ‘load’ the new project. Drumbit currently does not have the ability to export files to a more widely recognizable file-type, but it isn’t needed because any composition [...] options in drumbit

#### Possible Applications [...] Like Chrome Music Lab’s Song Maker and BeepBox, grooves composed in Groove Pizza can be shared through a link, but this app also easily integrates with Soundtrap. A rhythm track composed in Groove Pizza can be continued in Soundtrap without reformatting. It can also be transferred over to Noteflight and continued in that notation software as well. Currently there are no other platforms where it transfers as seamlessly; however, it can be transferred to pretty much any DAW with a few tweaks. For a DAW like BandLab, you could download as WAV or as MIDI but they would interact differently. If you export from Groove Pizza as WAV it becomes an audio file that cannot be altered once it is imported to a track in your DAW.
